concepts.def: Energy flow positions: producers (plants), primary consumers (herbivores), secondary (carnivores), tertiary, decomposers.
Biomass produced by plants after respiration; tropical rainforest highest (2200 g/m2/year), desert lowest.
Norman Myers' 36 regions with 1500+ endemic plants and 70%+ habitat loss; Madagascar, Cape Floristic, Indo-Burma.
Millennium Ecosystem Assessment 2005: provisioning (food, water), regulating (climate, pollination), cultural, supporting.
Breaking up of ecosystems into isolated patches by roads, farms; reduces species viability; e.g. Atlantic rainforest 12% remaining.
Sussex estate restored from intensive farming since 2001; reintroduced large herbivores; turtle dove, nightingale, purple emperor returned.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Ecosystems Under Stress — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Ecosystems Under Stress brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Ecosystems Under Stress.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
